summary.content:
Today's selection covers 61 articles from 8 trusted sources, including 35 on Artificial Intelligence and 14 on Fraud/Cybersecurity.

• **AI Spotlight**: Why students are being paid £2,000 to play computer games
• **Companies in Focus**: Coverage includes developments from OpenAI, Google, Anthropic
• **Security Alert**: Hackers infect Android car head units with proxy botnet malware
• **Threat Landscape**: Today's coverage highlights phishing, data breaches, malware
• **Source Diversity**: Articles sourced from BBC Technology, BleepingComputer, TechCrunch, NY Times Tech, Dark Reading and others
• **Fresh Content**: 10 articles published in the last 24 hours

top.title: Why students are being paid £2,000 to play computer games
top.description: Roehampton University offers students £2,000 a year to play esports alongside their studies.

top.title: Hackers infect Android car head units with proxy botnet malware
top.description: A supply-chain attack targeting Android-based car head units is using a legitimate device-update app to spread malware that enlists compromised devices in a proxy botnet or uses them for ad fraud. [.....

top.title: Inherent, founded by DeepMind alumni, says its AI ‘teammate’ just outperformed Anthropic and OpenAI at replicating research
top.description: Built by DeepMind alumni, British AI lab Inherent released Faraday, an AI agent whose ability to replicate scientific papers could be a stepping stone for innovation.

top.title: OpenAI says California should strengthen its AI safety bill
top.description: OpenAI is calling for California to strengthen SB 53, an AI safety bill that the company previously opposed.

top.title: How Big Tech Captured American Schools
top.description: Companies like Google and Microsoft have used their money, their might and their massive reach to influence nearly every step of the education supply chain.

top.title: The Data Center Backlash Bursts Into the Midterms
top.description: With opposition to the centers mounting, many Democrats and a growing number of Republicans are campaigning against them.
